content:
I have always enjoyed talking to young minds. Their curiosity, willingness to learn, and fearless questions often make a session as enriching for the trainer as it is for the participants.

Recently had the pleasure of conducting an online Public Speaking session for around 50 enthusiastic members of the Rotaract Club of Jyoti Nivas College, Bengaluru.

The session focused on three fundamental aspects of becoming an effective speaker—structuring a speech, overcoming fear and anxiety, and understanding the importance of consistent practice.

While public speaking techniques can certainly be taught, what truly stood out during this session was the participants' eagerness to understand the why behind every concept. Their inquisitive questions sparked meaningful discussions, making the session highly interactive and engaging. It was encouraging to see students challenge conventional thinking, seek practical solutions, and actively participate throughout the program. The positive feedback received at the end was both humbling and gratifying.

Public speaking is no longer just a skill reserved for leaders, anchors, or professional speakers. For students, it is an essential life skill that influences academic success, career opportunities, leadership potential, and personal confidence. Whether presenting a project, participating in group discussions, attending placement interviews, pitching an idea, or leading a team, the ability to communicate thoughts with clarity and confidence can create opportunities that technical knowledge alone often cannot.

Like any worthwhile skill, public speaking is not about eliminating nervousness—it is about learning to manage it. Confidence is built one speech at a time, one audience at a time, and one practice session at a time. Every great speaker was once a beginner who simply chose to keep speaking.

My sincere thanks to the Rotaract Club of Jyoti Nivas College for the opportunity to interact with such an energetic and motivated group of students. I wish each participant continued success as they find their unique voice and use it to make a positive impact.
